failures.question: Among customers who bought in both 2010 and 2011, how many spent less in 2011 than in 2010?
failures.example_sql: WITH yearly_spend AS (SELECT s.customer_id, d.year, SUM(s.revenue) AS total_revenue FROM fact_sales s JOIN dim_date d ON s.date_key = d.date_key WHERE d.year IN (2010, 2011) GROUP BY s.customer_id, d.year), customer_years AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2010 THEN total_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS spend_2010, SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2011 THEN total_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS spend_2011, COUNT(DISTINCT year) AS years_bought FROM yearly_spend GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT count(*) AS customers_spent_less FROM customer_years WHERE years_bought = 2010 AND spend_2011 < spend_2010

failures.question: What percentage of gross sales value was cancelled in 2011?
failures.example_sql: SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(ABS(SUM(c.revenue)), 0) * 100.0 / SUM(s.revenue), 2) AS cancellation_percentage FROM fact_sales s JOIN dim_date d ON s.date_key = d.date_key LEFT JOIN fact_cancellations c ON EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.invoice_date) = 2011 AND s.stock_code = c.stock_code AND s.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE d.year = 2011

failures.question: Which 5 customers had the highest net revenue after cancellations, and what was it?
failures.example_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, SUM(s.revenue) + COALESCE(SUM(cn.revenue), 0) AS net_revenue FROM dim_customer c JOIN fact_sales s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id LEFT JOIN fact_cancellations cn ON c.customer_id = cn.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY net_revenue DESC LIMIT 5

failures.question: Which month of 2011 brought in the most new customers (first-ever purchase), and how many?
failures.example_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(d.month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month, COUNT(c.customer_id) AS new_customers FROM dim_customer c JOIN dim_date d ON DATE_TRUNC('month', c.first_invoice_date) = d.month_start WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.first_invoice_date) = 2011 GROUP BY d.month_start ORDER BY new_customers DESC LIMIT 1
